svg.text: ONE COMPLETE DISTRICT · PLAN, ROUTES, SIGHTLINES, FOUR VIEWS · BOARD 01
Not a concept sheet. The proof: every discovery from Sheets 01–06 living together in one believable place. Spaces lead; buildings follow; the ground is always hinted, never dominant.
plan 1:1250-ish · views at the resident’s eye height (34/6.5) from the marked cones
Mornings need a destination. The square is exactly the size of a
queue that wants to talk; the road steps aside for it.
Stands at the square’s exit, not its centre — news
travels on the way to somewhere. It heralds the green (hinge from
The green was here first; every street bends around it, which is
why every sightline finds it. The district’s breath and its
Compression by consent: shops need each other, so awnings nearly
touch and both accents arrive at once. One floodlight sits in the
gap between buildings — the town’s quietest promise
South side, terrace facing the green: coffee watches the town go
by. The chair is the point; the coffee is the excuse.
The widest floor in town, deliberately empty six days a week so
that Friday feels like an event and every other day belongs to
One building, two duties: its front door faces the market square
(Friday), its gable faces Stadium Road (Saturday). THE HOME END
On the square’s edge, not in a lay-by — arrival lands
in the middle of life. The first thing a visitor sees is the
market, the pub, and the Oak beyond.
Deliberately the plainest street in the district: hedges, a rail,
two scarves. The quietest street carries the loudest hour, and
the square opens off the lane; the notice board stands at its exit, and the Oak is already visible beyond
compression: awnings nearly touch — and one floodlight sits exactly in the gap between the stores and the end house
MARKET SQUARE · THE PUB · THE BUS STOP
the widest floor in town; the pub’s one door serves Friday and Saturday; arrival lands in the middle of life
deliberately plain — hedges, a rail, two scarves; the quietest street carries the loudest hour

Every discovery is load-bearing — Sheet 01 frames every space · Sheet 02’s voice is every building · Sheet 03’s care dresses bakery, café and pub · Sheet 04 paves the ground · Sheet 05’s places are the rooms · Sheet 06’s rhythm strings them.

COMPRESSION → RELEASE, CONTINUOUS — lane » bakery square ○ » green (widest) ○ » high street (tightest) » market ○ » stadium road — and the ground is never seen whole: one floodlight in a gap (S2), two over the hedge (V4), sound before sight on matchday.
SHEETS 01–06 PROVED THE WORDS · DISTRICT 01 PROVES THE SENTENCE
